brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Build has level 0 (5 bases + 1 half) and level 1 (piece:0,0,1;full + piece:-1,0,1;full with snap:0,0,0;full), but check_build reports UNSUPPORTED for piece:-1,0,1;full and LOOSE_BODY for piece:-1,0,0;-1,1,0 – the -1,0 column is not locked to the main body, so upper storey is not verified as supported.
Added bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full and bin:-1,0,1~hex-bin-full on level 1 via apply sockets s240/s216; present in get_build.

No drawer socket offered at any stage – find_sockets drawer returned 0 total throughout (requires half base cut face; configurator returned note: place half base then no placement). Half bases half-e and half-w at 1,0,0 were tried, still 0 offers. No drawer was applied; instruction forbade guessing raw ops or starting new structure in final turns.

capOpenFaces applied in last apply, added 23 caps (cap:-1,0,0;* etc, cap:1,0,0;#;0 etc). find_sockets cap now shows only 26 open faces but capped as far as configurator allows; lockJoints also applied.

finish.summary: Built 7 bases over two levels with two hex-bin-full bins on the upper level and capOpenFaces/lockJoints executed. Drawer remains unplaced because configurator offers no drawer placement on this build, and the -1,0 column is flagged UNSUPPORTED/LOOSE_BODY – not fully verified.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
